description: What he knew, how he got it, and what he claimed about science. Fiction is cited only as what he wrote.

evidence_levels.documented: stated in a cited source (Verne's reported words, firsthand observation, or reliable reference)
evidence_levels.inferred: reasoned from multiple sources; see reasoning
evidence_levels.speculative: plausible but weakly or not supported by collected sources

records.claim: Repeatedly denied being a scientist or having studied science; called his knowledge reading-derived 'odds and ends'.

citations.quote: I may say that I have never studied science
I do not in any way pose as a scientist

records.claim: Read pencil in hand, kept classified notes (claimed ~20,000+), and read ~15-20+ newspapers plus scientific reviews daily.

citations.quote: I always read pencil in hand
I subscribe to over twenty newspapers

records.claim: Named readings: Revue Bleue, Revue des Deux Mondes, Cosmos, Tissandier's La Nature, Flammarion's L'Astronomie, Geographical Society bulletins, Le Tour du Monde; all of Reclus and Arago.
Geography was his declared passion and study, more than science.

citations.quote: geography is my passion and my study
I had always been devoted to the study of geography

records.claim: Loved watching machines since boyhood visits to the Indret works near Nantes.

citations.quote: I used to adore watching machines at work

records.claim: In 1893 held that steering balloons was impossible except in still air, and that if flight were solved it would be by a heavier-than-air machine on the bird principle. Made one balloon ascent at Amiens (with Godard).

citations.quote: I had no faith in the possibility of ever steering balloons
it will be with a machine which will be heavier than the air

records.claim: Dismissed claims that his inventions came true as 'mere coincidence' due to striving for realism.
The plot device of Le Tour du monde (gaining a day by crossing meridians) came from a newspaper item (Le Siècle) about circling the globe in 80 days.

citations.quote: I took up a copy of Le Siécle one morning
I could profit by a difference of meridian

records.claim: Claretie heard him explain how he combined letters to build ciphers the reader could not solve before the dénouement; Claretie saw 'du mathématicien' in him.

citations.quote: Il y a du mathématicien chez Jules Verne

records.topic: fiction as record of what he wrote
records.claim: His novels deploy contemporary science (balloons, submarines, projectiles, comets); these show what he wrote and researched, not personal predictions or beliefs.

citations.quote: cleverly prepared scientific and geographical details lent an air of versimilitude
